summary:
Rovers of the Solar System is a website developed to help people learn about the rovers in our solar system.
We built a platform that features a catalog of missions and rovers on the Moon and Mars, along with an interactive quiz with various questions. The answers to them can be found on the site. Our website was created for teenagers so they can easily learn about the rovers that have been launched into space.
Space archives and articles are usually boring for teenagers to read, and some of them can be unreliable sources of information. Our website is easy to read and uses verified sources, such as the NASA NSSDCA archives.
details:
Project Details: Rovers of Solar System

What does it do?

Rovers of Solar System is an interactive, popular-science web platform about the robotic explorers humanity has left on the Moon and Mars. Most of these rovers, landers and descent stages stopped working long ago, yet they are still sitting exactly where they landed. Our platform turns this abandoned equipment into an explorable museum for school students and teenagers. Users choose the Moon or Mars, explore an interactive 3D globe, zoom in on real landing sites and tap a spacecraft to learn its story. The catalog covers twelve missions to the Moon and Mars and the twelve vehicles that flew them.

How does it work?

Each spacecraft card combines:

A video of the mission’s landing or journey, with a voiceover (recorded by our team / created with ElevenLabs),

A short popular-science story about the mission’s goals, how the vehicle worked and what scientists learned from it,

The landing site and, where available, the trajectory or route.

The site also includes a quiz that explains every answer, a “Rovers and research vehicles” section on how these machines work, and a “Scientific sources” page.

Scientific accuracy

Accuracy was a core design principle. Our source is NASA’s NSSDCA archive. We clearly label what is real and what is reconstructed: Ingenuity’s final flight path is marked as a reconstruction from a NASA route file, not orbital imagery. Real measurements, models, diagrams and artistic illustrations are always labeled separately. The platform is an independent educational project and not an official NASA resource.

Benefits and intended impact

The history of robotic exploration is usually locked in technical databases and research papers that young people never open. We want to make it accessible, engaging and scientifically accurate for learners aged roughly 12–18. Rovers of Solar System runs in any browser, with no installation or login, so it works on a phone or a school computer. We are starting in Kazakhstan, home of the Baikonur Cosmodrome, and the platform is open to students worldwide.

Relevance to the challenge

This project responds directly to the “Abandoned Equipment on the Moon and Mars” challenge. Rather than treating this hardware as space junk, we present it as scientific and cultural heritage. Every abandoned rover and lander gets a precise place on the map and a story.

What makes it creative?

We combine three things that rarely appear together in one place for teenagers: interactive 3D planetary exploration, video content and first-person storytelling, in which each spacecraft tells its own story. Students don’t just read about a mission. They find it on another world, watch it and hear it.

Tools and technologies

Front end: (HTML, CSS, JavaScript; 3D library, e.g. Three.js / CesiumJS)

3D models: (Sketchfab / NASA 3D Resources)

Video: (video tools)

Voiceover: (team recordings / ElevenLabs)

Hosting: GitHub Pages

Data sources: NASA NSSDCA

What’s next

New worlds such as Venus, Titan, asteroid and comet landers, and a classroom mode with ready-made lessons for teachers.
